messages:
maria_sales: Kicking off the proof-of-concept with Acme. They report 401s on every inference call. Raised by the trial contact this morning.
acme_trial: Confirmed — curl returns 401 Invalid API key. We pasted the key from the welcome email into our app. No other errors in the app logs.
acme_trial: Example response: `{"error":"Invalid API key"}`. Using endpoint `https://api.redwood.inference/v1/inference`.
mar ia_sales: @tom_se can you join? I told them we'd swarm on auth keys.
 tom_se: On it. quick sanity checks: are they using the right header? should be `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` not `X-Api-Key`. Also confirm key prefix — hosted keys start with `rwd_` or `rwd-test_`.
acme_trial: we're doing `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`. Key starts with `rwd-test_`.
 n ina_platform: If it's `rwd-test_` it's a test key — check whether the PoC org/project is set up. 401 often when key belongs to a different org or has been rotated/disabled.
 acme_trial: How do we check? We don't see org/project in our console.
 tom_se: @acme_trial can you run this curl from terminal and paste the request id? `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/inference -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"hello"}'` Response headers include `x-rwd-request-id`.
 acme_trial: Here's response headers we got: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` then `x-rwd-request-id: rwd-req-00123abc` and body `{"error":"Invalid API key"}`
 nina_platform: Thanks. I'm pulling the request ID from logs... (checking).
 infra_bot: deploybot: looked up request rwd-req-00123abc — key fingerprint found, key status: active, bound_org: org_45, bound_project: prod-app.
 nina_platform: Interesting — the key is bound to org_45/prod-app. Are they attempting requests under a different org header or using a tenant header?
 acme_trial: We're not sending any org header. Just the bearer token. PoC was set up under Acme-POC org id — I think that's org_99.
 tom_se: That explains 401 — key belongs to org_45 but their account is under org_99. Two options: (1) generate a new key bound to org_99 and use that, or (2) we can rebind the existing key to org_99 from the console (requires admin).
 maria_sales: @acme_trial do you want us to create a temporary PoC key on your org? We can generate a scoped key for inference-only.
 acme_trial: Yes please. If you can generate a PoC-scoped key that would be fastest.
 nina_platform: I'll generate a short-lived key (48h) scoped to inference:generate and bound to org_99/proj-poc. Regenerating now...
 infra_bot: secrets-manager: created key rwd-test_poc_9f3a, status: active, scopes: [inference:generate], bound_org: org_99, bound_project: proj-poc, expires: 48h.
 nina_platform: New key created. @acme_trial please replace your old key with `rwd-test_poc_9f3a` and retry the same curl.
 acme_trial: Swapped in new key, retrying...
 acme_trial: Success! 200 OK, model responded. Thanks everyone.
 maria_sales: Great — next steps: we'll add a note in the PoC runbook that keys must be org-aligned and attachments for how to generate scoped PoC keys.
 tom_se: Also flagged potential UX improvement: console should show "key bound org" next to key list. I'll file a tiny ticket.
 maria_sales: Filing ticket would be great. @nina_platform can you attach the temporary key id to the PoC record?
 nina_platform: Done — linked rwd-test_poc_9f3a to PoC: ACME-2026-P1.
 acme_trial: One follow-up: earlier we also saw intermittent 429s at ~120rpm. Are there recommended defaults we should use for initial load?
 tom_se: For PoCs start with 40-60rpm, enable simple exponential backoff on 429s and use streaming where possible to reduce token usage. I'll DM a sample retry snippet. :thumbsup:
 maria_sales: Thanks everyone, closing the swarm. If any more auth/perms show up ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
